newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Currencies hit SKF sales, profits in Jan-Sept 1996.
newsitem.headline: Currencies hit SKF sales, profits in Jan-Sept 1996.

text.p: Swedish bearing manufacturer AB SKF posted on Thursday a 1.85 billion crown ($280 million) nine-month profit after financial items, and said foreign exchange items had dented sales and operating profits in the first three quarters of the year.
The figure represented a fall of 740 million crowns on the first nine months of last year, while sales fell by 10 percent to 25.36 billion crowns.

The result failed market expectations as a Reuter poll had established a market consensus of 1.99 billion crowns for the nine-month profit after financial items, and the share accordingly fell five crowns to close at 153.5 crowns.
The company said the decline in sales was due to structural changes, a fall in volumes and, first and foremost, the effects of a stronger Swedish currency.

"At the same time as reported sales decreased by about 2.5 billion crowns as a result of changes in exchange rates, operating income was also adversely affected by more than 500 million crowns for the same reasons," SKF said in a statement.
Operating profit fell to 2.16 billion crowns from 3.12 billion in the first nine months of 1995.
For the third quarter of the year in exclusion, the Gothenburg-based rolling bearing maker reported earnings of 374 million crowns, down from the 720 million shown in the third quarter of last year.

"The lower earnings for the third quarter...were due to a deterioration in the price and mix trend, a combination of continuing pressure on prices and a shift, particularly in western Europe, from profitable to less profitable customer segments," SKF said.
Nine-month profits for the rolling bearings division amounted to 1.66 billion crowns, down from the 2.19 billion crowns noted in the same period last year.
There was no general upturn in demand in western Europe, SKF said, but higher new car sales meant that deliveries to this customer segment had increased during the third quarter.

SKF's growth in the U.S. had continued, the company said, but the growth rate had slowed. However, deliveries to truck makers in the region had been significantly below last year's levels due to lower production among customers.

Profits of the Seals division dipped to 127 million crowns for the first three quarters from 156 million in the same 1995 period, while the Specialty Steels Unit noted a collapse in earnings to 52 million crowns from 230 million.
SKF said it expected the business climate to remain largely unchanged over the coming few quarters. ($ = 6.576 Swedish Crowns)
